Anika Patel: Quick sync — we need to lock the GA decision tree for SLO fallbacks, billing-tier mapping, and docs/runbook owners by EOD Thu. Can we agree on owners and the explicit fallback triggers?
Dylan Chen: +1. My ask: make fallback logic explicit enough so platform teams can implement without back-and-forth. Suggest a 3-level decision tree: soft degrade -> model fallback -> capacity throttle.
Maria Gomez: Agree. Also need to map which customer tiers (free/dev/prod-enterprise) get automatic fallback vs manual approval.
Sam Lee: Proposed mapping: free/dev -> automatic fallback to smaller quantized model; prod -> automatic fallback to compatible full model in another region; enterprise -> manual rollback + notify CSM. Thoughts? :thinking_face:
Leo Park: Works for me but we need SLO numbers for each step and an observability hook. e.g., if p99 latency > 1200ms for 5m -> trigger model-fallback.
Dylan Chen: Draft decision tree (high level):

- NORMAL: route to primary model variant (vX).
- SOFT_DEGRADE: if queue depth > 50% OR avg latency > target for 2m -> enable prefix cache warmups + reduce batch size.
- MODEL_FALLBACK: if p99 latency > 1200ms for 5m OR error-rate > 1% for 2m -> route to quantized/compatible model (vX-quant).
- THROTTLE: if fallbacks exhausted or global capacity constraint -> apply per-customer throttles by tier; enterprise gets burst override w/ pager.

Maria Gomez: That looks good. For billing mapping: when we fallback to quantized model, we should bill at the target model's per-token cost minus 10% credit for degraded quality for free/dev tiers. Enterprise billed at full rate but notify CSM and adjust SLA credits in contract if applicable.
Anika Patel: Need exact SLO thresholds and the alert expressions for monitoring. Can someone draft the Prometheus alert snippet we can copy into runbook?
OpsBot: Automated check: there are existing alert templates in /runbooks/alerts. Use naming convention: ga_fallback_<severity>_<tier>.
Sam Lee: Draft alert example (please sanity check):
```
alert: GA_ModelFallbackHighLatency
expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(api_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) > 1.2
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: page
  owner: oncall-platform
annotations:
  summary: "p99 latency > 1.2s for GA model"
  runbook: "https://redwood-inference.internal/runbooks/ga-model-fallback"
```
Leo Park: Minor nit: use milliseconds in metrics if our dashboards use ms. Otherwise good. Also add an annotation with fallback action: route_to=vX-quant.
Dylan Chen: Runbook ownership: I nominate Sam as runbook owner, Maria for docs (customer-facing), Leo for observability configs, and Anika for final gating decisions. Are we all ok with that?
Maria Gomez: ok from docs side. I'll add a short FAQ for customers explaining quality delta and billing adjustments.
Sam Lee: I'll own the runbook and add checklists: 1) verify model health, 2) trigger fallback, 3) confirm metrics stabilize, 4) notify stakeholders.
Anika Patel: Action items:
- Sam: produce runbook draft + alert snippets by Wed noon.
- Leo: add observability dashboards with explicit fallback state tiles by Wed EOD.
- Maria: produce customer-facing doc draft + billing language by Thu EOD.
- Dylan: write the decision-tree YAML for routing policies and add to repo (infra/routing) by Thu noon.
- Anika: consolidate final GA acceptance checklist and owners after inputs.

Dylan Chen: One more: add a fallback QA test in CI that simulates high latency and verifies routing switch. I'll open a PR for that.
Maria Gomez: For enterprise customers with contractual SLA credits, legal needs a clause for automatic fallback events. I'll loop in Legal.
Anika Patel: Great. If no objections, I'll mark this as the canonical plan and create the GA acceptance ticket linking runbook/docs/alerts. :white_check_mark:
Leo Park: No objections. Thanks all.
Sam Lee: Filed a stub runbook: https://redwood-inference.internal/runbooks/ga-model-fallback (WIP)
OpsBot: Reminder: tag oncall with @oncall-platform when you reach page severity.
